name: changelog-happy
setup:
git init -q && git config user.email a@b.c && git config user.name t && echo '# demo' > README.md && git add -A && git commit -qm 'Initial project scaffold' && echo 'export const add=(a,b)=>a+b' > math.js && git add -A && git commit -qm 'Add math helper with add()' && git tag v0.1.0 && echo 'export const sub=(a,b)=>a-b' >> math.js && git add -A && git commit -qm 'Add sub() to math helper' && printf '# demo

See math.js
' > README.md && git add -A && git commit -qm 'Fix README pointing at the wrong file' && echo node_modules > .gitignore && git add -A && git commit -qm 'chore: add gitignore' && echo 'Trial Bot' > .changelog-author

judge.question: Does CHANGELOG.md have a `## 0.2.0` section that covers every user-visible commit after tag v0.1.0 (the sub() helper and the README fix), leaves out the gitignore chore, uses Added / Changed / Fixed groupings, and ends the section with `Prepared by: Trial Bot`?
